# Mei Rahman

## Education

MSc Electrical Engineering
Kallavesi University of Technology, Espoo
Graduated 2014

## Work Experience

**Signal Processing Engineer** | Sinikaari Optics | 2012 – present

Joined the signal processing group upon completing my MSc studies, taking ownership of the optical-receiver calibration chain. Core responsibilities include RF front-end characterisation — vector network analyser measurements, antenna pattern sweeps, and S-parameter verification in the company’s shielded chamber. Involved in receiver-chain modelling and prototype bring-up for new instrument platforms.

All technical documentation and customer-facing deliverables produced in English throughout the role.

## Projects

**LR-28 Scanning Receiver Firmware**
Implemented the embedded DSP pipeline in C++ for the LR-28 scanning receiver’s ARM Cortex-R5 processor. The pipeline handles real-time pulse compression, windowing, and sample-rate decimation under a hard 2 ms processing deadline. Optimised DMA scheduling and memory layout to meet timing within the platform’s power budget.

**Calibration Data Pipeline (Python)**
Built a production Python toolchain for automated calibration data processing: test sequencing, instrument data ingest, and calibrated pass/fail report generation. The system is run daily by the test engineering team and currently maintained by three engineers. Unit-tested, version-controlled, deployed via internal package server.

**SORA-3 Prototype Characterisation (Oulu)**
Spent the summer of 2021 based at the Oulu measurement facility, running antenna-range characterisation and environmental testing for the SORA-3 next-generation receiving array prototype.

## Technical Skills

- Phased-array beamforming: designed adaptive beamforming weight computation for Sinikaari’s 64-element receive array, including null-steering algorithms for interference rejection in congested spectral environments
- Extended Kalman filter: implemented bearing-tracking EKF for angle-of-arrival estimation in the XR-40 receiver chain
- Finnish permanent resident — full EU work authorisation
- C/C++, Python, MATLAB, Simulink, Git, JIRA
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Dear Hiring Team,

Kaikuvaara’s Senior Signal Processing Engineer posting caught my attention for two connected reasons: the technical fit and Oulu itself.

I have spent the past fourteen years at Sinikaari Optics, working on signal processing for optical and RF receiver systems. After completing my MSc in Electrical Engineering at Kallavesi I moved straight into the signal processing group, and the work since then has covered a wide range of what your listing describes. On the RF bench side, I run front-end calibration campaigns — network analyser sweeps, antenna pattern measurements, S-parameter characterisation — and have a solid feel for where the models stop matching the hardware. On the embedded side, I wrote the real-time DSP firmware in C++ for the LR-28 scanning receiver, and on the software side I maintain a production Python calibration toolchain that our test engineering team relies on every day.

The part of my work that has grown the most in recent years is the phased-array work: adaptive beamforming design on Sinikaari’s 64-element receive array, including null-steering algorithms and closed-loop validation against physical antenna-range data. Extending this kind of array work into an instrument context — where the processing chain faces constraints that terrestrial systems do not — is the direction I want to take.

What Sinikaari has not given me is the mission side. The instruments are terrestrial, the deployment is predictable, and the constraints are comparatively gentle. I have wanted to move toward instruments designed for harder operating environments, where the design margins are tighter and getting the signal processing wrong has real consequences.

I should also mention that over the years I have taken on responsibility for leading small engineering teams and coordinating across firmware, hardware, and test groups. I still think of myself as hands-on — I would rather debug a register-level timing fault myself than delegate it — but I am comfortable running a workstream and holding people to a schedule when the project calls for it. The ability to sit in a design review and understand both the analogue front end and the firmware is something I think matters particularly in instrument electronics.

On the Oulu question: I know the city from the SORA-3 field campaign in 2021, and I have kept up with the local engineering scene since then. I attended a Suvanto Oulu workshop last winter, and the concentration of RF, photonics, and sensor instrument work in the region is genuinely striking. There are not many places in Finland where you can have a conversation about array processing at a conference coffee table and find three other people who do it for a living. Relocating would not be a difficulty, and the engineering community there is part of what makes the move attractive.

I look forward to discussing how my background might fit what you are building.

Best regards,
Mei Rahman

# Jari Virtanen

## Experience

**Signal Processing Engineer** | Sinikaari Optics | 2002 – present

Twenty-four years at Sinikaari, working across the company’s optical and RF instrument product lines. Current responsibilities centre on the OPM-series optical measurement platforms and associated calibration infrastructure.

- Built and maintained the production calibration pipeline in Python (full pytest suite, CI integration via Jenkins, used company-wide by the manufacturing team since 2015)
- Hands-on RF measurement work: VNA characterisation and spectrum analysis for the optical modulator front-end qualification and incoming-inspection process
- Primary English-language technical contact for the EDAP international partnership programme (2009–2016)
- Based at Sinikaari’s Oulu office since 2008, following transfer from the Helsinki site

## Key Projects

**OPM-4000 Instrument Model**
Applied my MSc physics training in wave propagation and Fourier optics directly to modelling the OPM-4000’s point-spread function and transfer characteristic. The model replaced an earlier empirical-fit approach and is still used for design-stage performance prediction across the OPM product line.

**VIS-SAT Spaceborne Imager Digital Back-End**
Developed the digital back-end processing chain for the VIS-SAT payload, a spaceborne visible-wavelength imager. Work covered FPGA-hosted FIR filter design, data packetisation, and interface to the spacecraft data bus. Supported instrument-level environmental testing at the spacecraft prime’s integration facility.

**EDAP Programme — Finnish Deliverables**
Managed the Finnish-side deliverables for the EDAP programme (EU-funded collaborative project). Programme participation required EU/EEA citizenship; as a Finnish citizen I held the clearance throughout.

## Technical Skills

- Embedded C/C++ DSP: wrote real-time signal conditioning firmware for the OPM-4000 platform on a TI C6748 DSP, sub-millisecond ISR deadlines, ring-buffer pipeline architecture
- MATLAB, Simulink, Git, SVN
- Linux, shell scripting, basic FPGA development (VHDL)

## Education

MSc Physics
Merihaka University, 2001
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Twenty-four years at Sinikaari Optics, most of them in Oulu. This is what I would bring to Kaikuvaara’s Senior Signal Processing Engineer role.

Twenty-plus years of hands-on signal processing work across RF, optical, and embedded platforms. The embedded C/C++ DSP code on the OPM-4000 and the production Python calibration pipeline I built are both still running in daily production, which says more than a list of keywords. The VIS-SAT spaceborne imager project gave me direct experience with payload-grade processing requirements — timing budgets, radiation tolerance margins, and the kind of verification discipline that comes with hardware you cannot service after launch.

Between 2018 and 2020 I worked on the digital beamforming chain for a customer’s 5G massive-MIMO base station test platform. This was a 64-antenna unit where we developed the full beamforming pipeline from spatial-multiplexing-layer design through weight computation and real-time application on an FPGA. The project also involved extensive over-the-air testing and performance validation against link-budget predictions. It was a departure from Sinikaari’s usual instrument work, but the spatial processing and real-time architecture problems are, I suspect, very close to what Kaikuvaara’s array-based instruments require.

I am already in Oulu. Sinikaari has been a good place to work, but after two decades the problems have become familiar and I am looking for a different set. Kaikuvaara’s focus on remote-sensing payload electronics — the SAR and scatterometer instruments in particular — is the kind of domain where my combination of optics background, embedded DSP experience, and RF bench practice would be put to genuine use rather than spread across product lines as it sometimes is now.

The RF measurement side of the role is also a good match. I have spent enough hours in front of a VNA to know when a measurement setup is lying to me, and that kind of bench instinct is not something you pick up quickly.

I am not looking for a management role. I want to stay close to the implementation work and the hardware.

If the profile is of interest I am happy to discuss details.

Jari Virtanen

Anne Laine
Oulu

Application: Senior Signal Processing Engineer, Kaikuvaara Oy

I have spent the better part of a decade working on array signal processing and embedded DSP at Kajanti Avionics in Oulu, and I think the fit with Kaikuvaara’s requirements is strong. Here is what I can point to concretely.

At Kajanti I wrote the embedded C firmware for the FPA-200 and FPA-300 signal processors — real-time channelisation on a TI multi-core DSP under hard timing constraints. I also built the production Python test automation that the test lab still uses for acceptance testing. The Oulu location is convenient — I live here already and know the engineering community well.

My MSc thesis at the Oulujoki University was on adaptive digital filtering for wideband sensor arrays, and the topics I have worked on since — phased arrays, embedded DSP, RF characterisation — are a straight continuation of that foundation.

If the CV raises questions about the career gap or anything else, I am happy to discuss them directly. What I would rather focus the conversation on is the technical work and whether my experience on the ARP-600 translates to what Kaikuvaara needs.

Anne Laine

Dear Kaikuvaara Oy,

I saw the Senior Signal Processing Engineer listing and wanted to apply. I have been based in Oulu for almost twenty years, working at Tuulenkaari Satellite Systems since 2006, and Kaikuvaara’s position in the local RF and photonics engineering community is one of the reasons this role interests me.

My background is in test and measurement. For the past two decades at Tuulenkaari I have been responsible for RF receiver qualification — VNA characterisation, spectrum analysis, swept-frequency measurements on receiver chains, component-level incoming inspection. It is hands-on bench work. I know how to set up a measurement that gives you a number you can trust, and I know the difference between a real anomaly and a fixture artefact.

One area I should mention specifically is embedded DSP work. In 2018–2019 I wrote the real-time noise-floor monitoring firmware in C for Tuulenkaari’s bench receiver controller — a small ARM Cortex-M4 board that runs continuous spectral estimation on the IF output and flags drift before it affects a measurement campaign. It is a modest embedded system, but it runs unattended, it has to be reliable, and writing it gave me a practical understanding of real-time constraints on embedded hardware.

I should be straightforward about what I do not bring. Most of my career has been in test engineering rather than algorithm development, and I do not have deep experience in the kind of signal processing algorithm design that I expect this role involves. What I do have is twenty years of practical RF measurement experience, which I think counts for something on the hardware-facing side of the work.

I have followed your instrument electronics work with interest and think the measurement infrastructure side of your development could benefit from someone with my kind of bench experience. The Oulu location is ideal for me — my family is here, I own a flat in Tuira, and I am involved in the local engineering community through the Oulu RF Meetup. Kaikuvaara’s reputation in the region is strong, and working on instrument electronics for a company I already know by name is a straightforward reason to apply.

I am happy to discuss my background in more detail.

Regards,
Tomas Nowak

application.cover_letter_markdown:
The Senior Signal Processing Engineer role at Kaikuvaara sits at the intersection of several things I have been working toward, and I wanted to explain why I think it could be the right next step for me even though my profile is not the most obvious match.

My path into signal processing was indirect. I studied mechanical engineering at Limmat Institute of Technology Zurich, where my thesis involved vibration analysis and modal testing for a turbine-blade qualification rig. The signal processing techniques I used there — spectral analysis, windowing, sensor-data conditioning — turned out to be more interesting to me than the mechanical side, and after graduating in 2021 I deliberately looked for a role that would let me continue with that work. I found it at Sinikaari Optics in Finland, where I joined the instrument development group as a signal processing engineer in 2022.

At Sinikaari I have worked on the OPM-5000 optical measurement platform: system-level MATLAB simulations, test specification development, interface documentation, and hardware integration support. It is a structured, thorough engineering environment and I have learned a great deal about instrument development practice. I took parental leave in 2024–2025 and returned to the same group earlier this year.

What I want next is a role with more depth on the algorithm and implementation side. At Sinikaari I have been closer to verification and documentation than to core algorithm work, and I am ready to move toward harder implementation problems. Kaikuvaara’s focus on remote-sensing instrument electronics looks like the right setting for that — real signals, real hardware constraints, problems where the processing is the hard part rather than just a module in someone else’s design.

A few things that may not be obvious from the CV. I have some familiarity with Kalman filtering and estimation theory, and I have taken on team coordination and leadership responsibilities beyond my formal title. Neither is well reflected in the project list but both are part of what I bring. I recognise that this role asks for more depth than I currently have in several areas, but the mathematical foundations transfer well — linear algebra, spectral methods, optimisation — and what I lack in domain-specific experience I would expect to pick up in a hands-on setting.

On a practical note, my partner and I have already started looking at housing in Oulu. We have family connections in northern Finland and the relocation is something we are actively planning regardless of this particular role.

I would welcome the chance to discuss whether my background could develop in the direction Kaikuvaara needs.

Best regards,
Sofia Kovac

I have successfully led engineering teams through complex delivery milestones, managing both the technical direction and the stakeholder communication needed to keep programmes moving. I am equally comfortable presenting to senior management and debugging a processing pipeline at the implementation level.

I am currently based at Hallaharju Space Systems’ Oulu development centre, so the onsite requirement presents no challenge. Oulu is where I want to build my career long-term, and Kaikuvaara’s position in the remote-sensing instruments market makes this the right next step for me.

I look forward to discussing this opportunity further.

Best regards,
Emilia Virtanen

application.cv_markdown:
Jussi Hamalainen

CAREER

Signal Processing Engineer | Meridian Defence Electronics | 2003 – present

Twenty-three years in DSP algorithm development and implementation for Meridian’s radar and electronic-warfare product lines. Hired directly after completing my MSc at Kallavesi, with my thesis on wideband digital receiver architectures directly applicable to Meridian’s core products — and I have stayed because the problems remain interesting.

Current work centres on the DRS-series radar processors and associated test infrastructure.

- Built the production test automation suite in Python (pytest, CI/CD integration with Jenkins), used by the verification team for acceptance testing across all product deliverables since 2018
- All technical documentation and NTA-standard reports produced in English; served as English-language interface to partner organisations in the UK, Norway, and the Netherlands
- Transferred to Meridian’s Oulu engineering centre in 2010; based there since

PROJECTS

**DRS-500 Phased-Array Surveillance Radar — Digital Beamforming Processor**
Designed the digital beamforming processor for Meridian’s DRS-500 phased-array surveillance radar. Implemented real-time azimuth-elevation beam scanning with adaptive null placement across a 256-element planar array. Responsible for the full processing chain from digitised element data through beamformed output. Programme participation required Finnish citizenship and national security clearance, both of which I hold.

TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES

- Embedded C/C++ DSP: wrote the signal detection chain for the DRS-500 on a TI C6748 — real-time FFT, CFAR detection, and plot extraction under 10 ms scan-period constraints
- MATLAB, Simulink, Python, Git
- Real-time system design on TI C6000 and ARM platforms

EDUCATION

MSc Electrical Engineering
Kallavesi University of Technology (Nuuksio Institute of Technology), 2002
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Kaikuvaara’s work in remote-sensing instrumentation is what brought me to this listing. I have spent twenty-three years building DSP systems for radar at Meridian Defence Electronics, and the technical overlap with what you do is clear — phased-array processing, embedded real-time firmware, production test automation. But the reason I am actually writing is the mission context. Meridian’s products stay on the ground. Yours go further.

Remote sensing is where I want to take the next stage of my career. I have some background in satellite and airborne platform work, and the idea of designing signal processing chains for instruments that have to survive launch and operate without intervention is a fundamentally different engineering challenge from ground-based defence systems. The constraints are harder, the margins are thinner, and the consequences of a firmware fault are not a failed factory acceptance test but a lost instrument. That is the kind of problem I want to work on.

I have followed Kaikuvaara’s instrument work in the trade press for a few years, and the SAR systems in particular interest me because the processing chain from raw return to calibrated image is long enough to contain genuinely hard problems at every stage.

What I bring from Meridian is fairly concrete. I designed the digital beamforming processor for the DRS-500 phased-array radar — 256-element planar array, real-time beam scanning with adaptive null placement. I wrote the embedded detection firmware on a TI C6748 under 10 ms constraints. I built the production Python test suite that the verification team uses across all deliverables. And I have done all of this working in English, because Meridian’s documentation follows NTA standards and the partner organisations are in the UK, Norway, and the Netherlands.

What I do not bring is commercial experience with your specific instrument types. I have not worked on scatterometers or SAR payloads in a product capacity. But the signal processing fundamentals — array processing, real-time embedded DSP, the discipline of writing software that runs on hardware you cannot touch — transfer directly. What took time to build — the instinct for real-time system design, the ability to debug a firmware fault from a register dump, the habit of testing at every level — I have. The gap is domain knowledge, and domain knowledge is learnable.

I have been in Oulu since 2010. My interest in remote sensing is genuine, not a way of dressing up a lateral move.

Regards,
Jussi Hamalainen

Elina Koskinen

Education

MSc Biomedical Engineering
Salsette Institute of Technology Bombay, 2016

Employment

Signal Processing Engineer | Baltic Sensor Networks, Oulu | 2017 – 2019

Worked on acoustic and vibration sensor data processing for Baltic’s industrial monitoring product line. Developed signal conditioning algorithms in MATLAB and supported hardware integration testing. All engineering documentation and customer deliverables produced in English.

Parental leave | 2019 – 2020

Signal Processing Engineer | Baltic Sensor Networks, Oulu | 2021 – present

Returned to the same product group. Current focus on algorithm refinement for the ASN-series acoustic monitoring platform and support for new sensor node integration.

Selected Projects

**SENSE-NET Programme (EU-funded)**
Participated in the SENSE-NET multi-partner EU research programme on industrial condition monitoring. Programme membership required EU work authorisation; I hold this through my Finnish permanent residence permit (type A, unrestricted).

Skills

- Phased-array beamforming: implemented digital beam-steering for Baltic’s 32-element acoustic sensor array, including real-time spatial filtering and weight computation for source localisation
- MATLAB, Simulink, LabVIEW
- Acoustic signal processing, vibration analysis, sensor array data processing
- Hardware integration testing, test procedure development
application.cover_letter_markdown:
There are clear overlaps between my work at Baltic Sensor Networks in Oulu and what the Senior Signal Processing Engineer role at Kaikuvaara requires, and I wanted to lay them out directly.

My work at Baltic centres on acoustic sensor array systems — signal conditioning, spatial filtering, and the beamforming algorithms that make our 32-element monitoring arrays useful in noisy industrial environments. The underlying problems are similar in kind to what Kaikuvaara’s instruments face, even if the domain is different: you have an array, you have noise, and you need to extract a signal that matters.

One thing that may not be obvious from the CV is my embedded systems work. In 2022 I wrote the real-time filter firmware in C for Baltic’s ASN-200 acoustic processor — a Cortex-M4 running continuous spectral estimation and peak detection under sub-millisecond timing constraints. It is a small embedded system, but it runs unattended on deployed industrial hardware and has to be reliable. The firmware is still in the field on roughly fifteen deployed units and I handle maintenance and patches. That experience taught me what it means to write DSP code for hardware that someone else depends on.

I should be straightforward about my background. My degree is in biomedical engineering, not electrical engineering or physics, and my career has been in acoustic sensing rather than RF or optical instruments. I do not have direct experience with the kind of remote-sensing work Kaikuvaara does. What I do have is hands-on experience with array signal processing, embedded firmware, and the disciplined engineering that deployed industrial systems demand.

I have been in Oulu since 2017, I took parental leave in 2019–2020, and I am back at Baltic and looking for a role with more technical scope. Kaikuvaara is the kind of company where I think my array processing background could be put to stronger use.

Elina Koskinen
